prompts.question: What is the primary efficacy endpoint, and in which analysis set is it tested primarily?

criteria.criterion: Correctly identifies OS as the primary endpoint
Correctly identifies ITT as the primary analysis set
Correctly states the OS definition as time from randomization to death due to any cause

prompts.question: Describe the randomization scheme and the stratification factors used in the study. Also identify which stratification factors are used in the primary efficacy analysis model/test.

criteria.criterion: Correctly identifies 1:1 randomization
Correctly identifies all 3 randomization stratification factors: region, ECOG 0 vs 1, ICC option
Correctly distinguishes that the primary efficacy analysis uses ECOG and ICC option, but not region, for stratified testing/modeling

prompts.question: What multiplicity control strategy is used, and what is the testing hierarchy across the primary and key secondary endpoints?

criteria.criterion: Correctly identifies one-sided alpha = 0.025
Correctly identifies that OS in ITT is tested first
Correctly identifies gatekeeping to OS in PD-L1 positive set only if OS in ITT is significant
Correctly describes strong familywise type I error control  at one-sided 0.025

prompts.question: Summarize the key assumptions used for the sample size calculation.

criteria.criterion: Correctly identifies target HR = 0.75
Correctly identifies power = 82%
Correctly identifies one-sided alpha = 0.025
Correctly identifies dropout rate = 5% per year
Correctly identifies approximately 500 patients, randomized 1:1
Correctly calculates approximately 400 deaths as target events

prompts.question: Using the study documents only, explain how the planned primary analysis timing is linked to the target event count and sample size design. What is the target number of deaths, and what assumptions support that target?

criteria.criterion: Correctly identifies approximately 400 deaths as the trigger for primary OS analysis
Correctly identifies at least 4 major supporting assumptions among HR, alpha, power, dropout, accrual duration, sample size, assumed median OS
Correctly links the target event count to sample size assumptions rather than presenting it as a standalone number

prompts.question: Describe the planned primary statistical analysis for OS, including hypothesis testing method, stratification, effect estimate, and summary outputs.

criteria.criterion: Correctly identifies one-sided stratified log-rank test for primary comparison
Correctly identifies analysis stratification factors as ECOG and ICC option
Correctly identifies Cox model as the treatment effect model
Correctly identifies HR with two-sided 95% CI as reported effect estimate
Correctly identifies KM curves and median OS summaries

prompts.question: How is PFS handled analytically, and what are the main censoring/event rules relevant to new anti-cancer therapy, loss to follow-up, and absence of progression at analysis?

criteria.criterion: Correctly identifies PFS as investigator-assessed per RECIST v1.1
Correctly identifies censoring at last tumor assessment when no progression/death at analysis
Correctly identifies censoring at last tumor assessment before new anti-cancer therapy
Correctly identifies stratified log-rank and stratified Cox as main analytical methods

prompts.question: Define treatment-emergent adverse event (TEAE) in this study, including the standard follow-up window and the special handling of immune-related AEs / drug-related SAEs.

criteria.criterion: Correctly identifies TEAE onset/worsening from baseline on or after first dose
Correctly identifies 30-day post-last-dose / until new anticancer therapy rule
Correctly identifies special 90-day rule for immune-related AEs regardless of new therapy
Correctly identifies special handling of drug-related SAEs after treatment discontinuation
